hints: Remember Le Chatelier's principle treats temperature and pressure separately, so check what each change favours for the forward reaction.
Increasing temperature favours the endothermic direction, so look for a reaction with positive $\Delta H$ for the forward reaction.
Decreasing pressure favours the side with more moles of gas, so count gas moles on left and right and find where both effects point right.
walkthrough:
**What does higher temperature do?**

Think of heat as a reactant or product. Increasing temperature shifts equilibrium away from heat, so it favours the endothermic direction.

Rule:
$$\text{increase T favours endothermic, decrease T favours exothermic}$$

**Apply the temperature rule**

For a shift to the right on heating, the forward reaction must be endothermic, meaning $\Delta H$ is positive.

That leaves:
$$\text{A: } \Delta H = +40 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1} \text{ (right)}$$ 
$$\text{B: } \Delta H = +58 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1} \text{ (right)}$$

**What does lower pressure do?**

Decreasing pressure favours the side with the larger number of moles of gas, because the system tries to make more particles to raise pressure back up.

Rule:
$$\text{decrease p favours side with more gas moles}$$

**Apply the pressure rule and conclude**

Count gas moles. A has 2 on the left and 2 on the right, so pressure has no effect. B has 1 mole $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$ on the left and 2 moles $\text{NO}_2$ on the right, so lower pressure shifts right.

Only the reaction where both temperature increase and pressure decrease shift right is the correct choice.

options.A: Temperature increase does shift this right because forward $\Delta H = +40 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ is endothermic. However gas moles are 2 on the left ($\text{H}_2 + \text{CO}_2$) and 2 on the right ($\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}$), so changing pressure has no effect.
options.B: Forward reaction is endothermic ($\Delta H = +58 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$) so increasing temperature shifts equilibrium to the right. Gas moles increase from 1 ($\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$) to 2 ($2\text{NO}_2$), so decreasing pressure also shifts equilibrium to the right to make more particles.
options.C: Forward reaction is exothermic ($\Delta H = -197 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$) so increasing temperature shifts equilibrium to the left, not right. Also gas moles decrease from 3 to 2, so decreasing pressure shifts left as well.
options.D: Forward reaction is exothermic ($\Delta H = -10 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$) so increasing temperature shifts equilibrium to the left. Gas moles are 2 on both sides ($2\text{HI}$ vs $\text{H}_2 + \text{I}_2$), so pressure change has no effect.
